questions.q: A car is negotiating a curved road of radius $\text{R}$. The road is banked at an angle $\theta$. The coefficient of friction between the tyres of the car and the road is ${\mu}_{s}$. The maximum safe velocity on this road is:
questions.solution:
$N = mgcos ⁡ \theta + \dfrac{mv^{2}}{R}sin ⁡ \theta$
${f}_\max = \muN ⇒{f}_\max = {μ}_{s}mgcos ⁡ \theta + \dfrac{{μ}_{s}mv^{2}}{R}sin ⁡ \theta$
$mg⁡ sin\theta + {f}_\max = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{R}⁡ cos\theta$
$mgsin ⁡ \theta + {μ}_{s}mgcos ⁡ \theta + \dfrac{{μ}_{s}mv^{2}}{R}sin ⁡ \theta = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{R}cos ⁡ \theta$
$gsin ⁡ \theta + {μ}_{s}gcos ⁡ \theta = \dfrac{v^{2}}{R} \left($cos ⁡ $\theta - {μ}_{s}$sin ⁡ $\theta\right)
$gR\left[\dfrac{tan ⁡ \theta + {μ}_{s}}{1 - {μ}_{s}tan ⁡ \theta}\right] =$v^{2}$

questions.q: Two blocks $A$ and $B$ of masses $3m$ and $m$ respectively are connected by a massless and inextensible string. The whole system is suspended by a massless spring as shown in figure. The magnitudes of acceleration of $A$ and $B$ immediately after the string is cut, are respectively
questions.solution:
Before the string is cut, tension is acting in the string in downward position.
$kx = T + 3mg$ ......(i)
$T = mg$ ......(ii)

$⇒ kx = 4mg$
After the string is cut, $T = 0$

$a = \dfrac{kx - 3mg}{3m}$
$a = \dfrac{4mg - 3mg}{3m}$
Acceleration of $A$is $a = \dfrac{g}{3} ↑$ and acceleration of $B$ is $a = \dfrac{mg}{m} = g ↓$.

questions.q: A roller coaster is designed such that riders experience "weightlessness" as they go round the top of a hill whose radius of curvature is $20 \mathrm{~m}$. The speed of the car at the top of the hill is between
questions.solution:
Balancing the forces, we get
M g-N=M $\frac{v^{2}}{R}$For weightlessness, $N=0\therefore\frac{M v^{2}}{R}=$M g where $R$ is the radius of curvature and $v$ is the speed of car. Therefore, v=$\sqrt{\mathrm{Rg}}$Putting the values, $R=20 \mathrm{~m}, g=10.0 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrms^{2}$ So, $\quad v=\sqrt{20 \times 10.0}=14.14 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrms^{2}$ Thus, the speed of the car at the top of the hill is $\text { between }$14 $\mathrm{~m}$/ $\mathrm{s} \text { and }$15 $\mathrm{~m}$/ $\mathrm{s} \text { . }$Note : The roller coaster is a popular amusement ride developed for amusement parks and modern theme parks.

questions.q:
A block of mass $10 \mathrm{~kg}$ is placed on a horizontal frictionless surface and is attached to a cord which passes over two light frictionless pulleys as shown in the figure. The hanging block tied to the other end of the cord is initially at rest $2 \mathrm{~m}$ above the horizontal floor.If the hanging block strikes the floor $2 \mathrm{~s}$ after the system is released, then weight of the hanging block is ....... \left(g=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}\right)$
$
questions.solution: For hanging block, $\begin{aligned}$& \quad s=u t+$\frac{1}{2}$a t²[\because u=0] \Rightarrow 2=$\frac{1}{2} \times$a $\times$2^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad a=1 $\mathrm{~ms}^{-2} \end{aligned}$So, velocity of hanging block $=$ velocity of $10 \mathrm{~kg}$ block after $2 \mathrm{~s}\begin{array}{ll} \Rightarrow$& v=u+a t \\ \Rightarrow & v=0+1 $\times$2 $\text { or }$v=2 $\mathrm{~ms}^{-1} \end{array}$From work - energy theorem, $\mathrm{KE}$ of $10 \mathrm{~kg}$ block $=$ Work done by gravity on hanging block $=\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 2^2=m \times 10 \times 2$ \Rightarrow \quad m=1 $\mathrm{~kg}$Weight of hanging block $=1 \times 10=10 \mathrm{~kg} \approx 11.1 \mathrm{lN}$

questions.q: The masses of blocks $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ are $\mathrm{m}$ and $\mathrm{M}$ respectively. Between $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$, there is a constant frictional force $\mathrm{F}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ can slide on a smooth horizontal surface. A is set in motion with velocity while $\mathrm{B}$ is at rest. What is the distance moved by A relative to B before they move with the same velocity?
questions.solution:
For the blocks A and B FBD as shown below

Equations of motion
$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{A}}=\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\mathrm{M}}(\text { in }-\mathrm{x} \text { direction }) \\
\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{B}}=\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\mathrm{M}}(\text { in }+\mathrm{x} \text { direction) }
\end{array}
Relative acceleration, of A w.r.t. B,
\begin{aligned}$
$\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}}$&=$\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{A}}-\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{B}}=-\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\mathrm{m}}-\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\mathrm{M}}$\\
&=-$\mathrm{F}\left(\frac{\mathrm{M}+\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{Mm}}\right)(\text { along }-\mathrm{x} \text { direction })$
\end{aligned}$
Initial relative velocity of A w.r.t. B, \mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{AB}}=\mathrm{v}_{0}
using equation $v^{2}=u^{2}+2$ as
$0=v_{0}^{2}-$\frac{2 \mathrm{~F}(\mathrm{~m}+\mathrm{M}) \mathrm{S}}{\mathrm{Mm}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{S}=\frac{\mathrm{Mmv}_{0}^{2}}{2 \mathrm{~F}(\mathrm{~m}+\mathrm{M})}
i.e., Distance moved by A relative to B
\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{AB}}=\frac{\mathrm{Mmv}_{0}^{2}}{2 \mathrm{~F}(\mathrm{~m}+\mathrm{M})}$

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct order of forces?
options: Weak force $<$ gravitational forces $<$ strong force (nuclear) $<$ electrostatic force
Gravitational force $<$ weak force~$<$(electrostatic)$<$ strong force
Gravitational force& $<$ electrostatic force$<$ weak force $<$ strong force
Weak force& $<$ gravitational force~$<$ electrostatic force$<$ strong force
questions.solution:
Strong nuclear force, electrostatic force, weak force and gravitational force are the four fundamental forces. Among these fundamental forces, strong nuclear forces which holds the two positive protons inside the nucleus are the strongest followed by electrostatic force. Also, gravitational force is weakest among all.

Hence, correct order of force is Gravitational force<Weak Nuclear Force<Electrostatic force<Strong nuclear force.

questions.q: A block of mass $10$ kg is in contact against the inner wall of a hollow cylindrical drum of radius$1m$. The minimum angular velocity needed for the cylinder to keep the block stationary when the cylinder is vertical and rotating about its axis will be \left(g = 10ms^{- 2}\right)
questions.solution:
$N = m{ω}^{2}R$
$f = mg$
For minimum angular velocity,
$f = \muN$
$mg = \mu \cdot m{ω}^{2}R$
$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{\muR}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{10}{0.1 \times 1}} = 10rads^{- 1}$

questions.q: In the figure, the mass of a ball is $\dfrac{9}{5}$ times the mass of the rod. Length of the rod is $1m$. The level of ball is the same as rod level. Find out the time taken by the ball to reach at the upper end of the rod.
questions.solution:
Let ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ be accelerations of a ball (upward) and rod (downward), respectively.



Clearly, from the diagram

$2{a}_{1} - {a}_{2}$ ...(i)

Now, for the ball

$2T - \dfrac{9}{5}mg - \dfrac{9}{5}ma$ ...(ii)

and for the rod, $mg - T = m{a}_{2}$ ...(iii)

On solving equations (i) and (iii), we get

${a}_{1} = \dfrac{g}{29}ms^{- 2} ↑$ (upward)

${a}_{2} = \dfrac{2g}{29}ms^{- 2} ↓$ (downward)

So, acceleration of ball w.r.t rod $= {a}_{1} + {a}_{2} = \dfrac{3g}{29}$

Now, displacement of ball w.r.t. rod when it reaches the upper end of rod is $1m$ .

Using the equation of motion,

$s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2}$

$s = 0 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{3 \times 10}{29}t^{2}$

$t = \sqrt{\dfrac{58}{30}} = 1 .4 s \left(approx\right)$

questions.q: The friction coefficient between the board and the floor shown in diagram is $\mu$. Find the maximum force that the man can exert on the rope, so that the board does not slip on the floor.
questions.solution:
The forces acting on the system are shown in the diagram

For vertical equilibrium of the point $P$

$T = F$ ....(i)



And for the vertical equilibrium of the system



$R + T = ( m + M ) g$, i.e., $R = ( m + M ) g - T$ ....(ii)

Now the system will not move horizontally till

$T < {f}_{L}$

i.e., $T < \mu [ \left(m + M\right)g - T ] \left({f}_{L} = \muR\right)

which on simplification gives

$T < \mu \left(\text{m} + \text{M}\right)\text{g} \left($1 + \mu\right)$

So in the light of equation (i), we get

${F}_\max = \mu \left(\text{m} + \text{M}\right)\text{g} \left(1 + \mu\right)$

questions.q: A car moves uniformly along a horizontal sine curve $y = asin ( x / \alpha )$, where $a$ and $\alpha$ are certain constants. The coefficient of friction between the wheels and the road is equal to $k$. The maximum constant speed at which the car can travel without sliding is
questions.solution:
Step I : Determine the radius of curvature of given curve at point P (x, y).

∵ $y = a \text\sin \dfrac{x}{\alpha} ∴ \dfrac{d ⁡ y}{d ⁡ x} = \dfrac{a}{\alpha} \text\cos \dfrac{x}{\alpha}$

∴ $\dfrac{{d ⁡}^{2} y}{d ⁡ x^{2}} = - \dfrac{a}{{α}^{2}} \text\sin \dfrac{x}{\alpha}$

∴ the radius of curvature is $R ⁡ = \dfrac{{\left[1 + {\left(\dfrac{d ⁡ y}{d ⁡ x}\right)}^{2}\right]}^{3 / 2}}{\dfrac{{d ⁡}^{2} y}{d ⁡ x^{2}}}$

$R ⁡ = \dfrac{{\left[1 + \dfrac{a^{2}}{{α}^{2}} \cos^{2} \dfrac{x}{a}\right]}^{3 / 2}}{- \dfrac{a}{{α}^{2}} \text\sin \dfrac{x}{\alpha}}$ ...(i)

Step II: Relate the friction and centripetal acceleration. In this case, centripetal acceleration is provided by force of friction.

∵ $f \le {f}_{L}$ or$f \le kmg$

or $\dfrac{{mv}^{2}}{R ⁡} \le \text{kmg} \text{or} \dfrac{{v ⁡}^{2}}{R ⁡} \le \text{kg}$

∴ $\dfrac{{v ⁡}_\max^{2}}{{R ⁡}_\min} = k \text{g}$

∴ ${v ⁡}_\max = \sqrt{k \text{g} {R ⁡}_\min}$

From equation (i), for the minimum value of the radius of curvature,

$\dfrac{x}{\alpha} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

∴ ${R ⁡}_\min = \dfrac{{α}^{2}}{a}$ (from equation. (i))

∴ ${v ⁡}_\max = \sqrt{\dfrac{k \text{g} {α}^{2}}{a}} = \alpha \sqrt{\dfrac{k \text{g}}{a}}$
